newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids values surge on oil, natgas rally.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids values surge on oil, natgas rally.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel oil prices finished sharply higher Thursday, moving in line with a rally in crude and natural gas prices, market sources said.
The entire resid complex, in both the paper and physical markets, surged following recent strength in the high sulphur materials due to firm bunker demand.
"We have the bunker market supporting those prices," said one Houston trader.
There may a sign in the low-sulphur end of the resid spectrum after Niagara Mohawk Power Corp issued a tender today seeking up to 350,000 barrels of fuel oil.
NYH physical one percent was assessed $20.50 a barrel, up from Wednesday's $19.00 a barrel, with early October paper quote at $20.20-$20.45 versus Wednesday's $19.55-$19.80.
NYH spot three percent jumped to $19.25, sharply higher than $17.25 on Wednesday.
NYMEX November crude futures settled up 76 cents at $24.81 a barrel and November Henry Hub natgas futures ended up 16.6 cents at $2.346 per million British thermal units.
At the Gulf, spot one percent sulphur rose to $18.88 a barrel, up from Wednesday's $17.48 and three percent was valued at $18.75, up from $17.25 on Wednesday.
October New York City Gate natural gas was assessed near $2.45/mmBtu, up from Wednesday's range of $2.22-$2.26, compared with NYH one percent resid at $3.25/mmBtu equivalent.
